One of the best roguelikes and one of the only ones I've been properly able to get into.

The gameplay is simple, but hard to master. It has lot of variety with lots of different bosses and routes that you do with all the different characters who all feel unique. Progression stills exists hundreds of hours into gameplay as you steadily build up unlocks which keep things fresh and entertaining even after getting every ending. The difficulty remains constant throughout the game with careful gameplay being rewarded with more chances to get powerful items and clever item choices being rewarded with easier gameplay. The sound design and music are also good which makes the whole experience even better. Everything works together really well; the only problems I have are that some items don't really synergise with others as well as they should and it can be really hard to see the shadows for enemies that drop from the sky. These can both be fixed with mods though.

The game also has a story which isn't anything revolutionary, but still pretty good. The story is primarily illustrated through the theming of the different items and some short cutscenes. It's what gives the game it's unique identity and contributes towards it's deserved status as one of the classics of the genre or perhaps even the medium as a whole.

This is the type of game I have wishlisted for a long long time and then end up getting it gifted one day cuz "why not?" and actually end up enjoying it.

The game is definitely something I'd call a classic, it's been out for such a long time that my review won't exactly give any more information that there already is, hence why I was hesitant to write it in the first time. It's another roguelike (we love em), a very effective one at that. The amount of items and characters and challenges available even just in base game is insane, I never felt like I was getting bored (not that it's easy to stay nonchalant when everything is shooting your ass) and the more you achieve, the deeper you get to progress.

In fact, what left me a bigger impression was not the gameplay itself but the art and the story- it is all so grotesque yet at the same time I feel so curious to understand what can each entity represent. The religious elements, the nudity/exposure of both outside skin and inside organs makes me feel so bad for Isaac, knowing he's just a child filled with so much fear and shame, the more items he picks up which can either be something like maybe cool sounding to just something related to the idea that he is disgusting, stained with his own sins. While my family was never this extremely religious, small part of me relates to how awful it can make you feel. 

This is something no child should ever go through and it weirdly reminds me of Stephen King's "Carrie". Both being made to feel like they are monsters and nothing more, both having fanatical mothers raise them to think exactly this and, of course, symbolism of blood. The story, for how simple it seems at first, it extremely tragic and has great visual perception of how a child cannot differentiate neglect/emotional and physical abuse and tries to embody it into something more understandable to the child: monsters, devils, spikes. I don't want to exactly spoiler anything but [spoiler]finding out that isaac suffocated in that very chest he hid in and all the dungeon runs were just his imagination during his last moments is really dark[/spoiler] but I think the story would not be the same if that wasn't the case. 

Overall, a game that should be talked about, easy replayability, great story, charming artstyle and the gameplay is not hard to learn but it is hard to master. If you are unsure if this is your cup of tea, you can buy it during a sale and try it out, earlier runs don't take too much time compared to later stuff you end up doing just for a new item and ending :)
